repo_notes.content: SqlArtisan is a type-safe SQL query builder for C# (.NET 8): you write SQL-like C# and it produces the SQL string plus its bind parameters.

Core principle: 'The SQL you write is the SQL that runs.' SqlArtisan emits SQL faithfully with NO cross-dialect rewriting or translation. Cross-database portability is a deliberate non-goal — never describe SqlArtisan as a portability or abstraction layer over databases.

Supported dialects: MySQL, Oracle, PostgreSQL, SQLite, SQL Server (default: PostgreSQL). Dialect differences are confined to the dialect layer (IDbmsDialect under src/SqlArtisan/Internal/SqlBuilder/DbmsDialect: alias quoting, parameter markers, string-literal escaping and a few statement-shape tokens); function nodes never branch on the target DBMS. A construct a dialect lacks is a separate, dialect-named API, never a rewrite.

Mission: a deterministic guard rail for SQL written alongside generative AI, built as four layers — (1) types: invalid builder chains fail to compile; (2) a bundled Roslyn analyzer (SQLA0001–SQLA0304) that flags configuration errors, unsupported constructs, version shortfalls, context-restricted positions, unaliased correlated DML targets, C# operator fallbacks that bind a value instead of SQL, comparisons with NULL that are never true, nameof aliases no Dapper model member takes, over-long identifiers, and schema contradictions read from the generated table classes at build time; (3) exact-SQL unit tests that pin the emitted SQL; (4) an integration-test matrix verified against live database engines.
Opinions live in docs and the analyzer, never in API holes: no legitimate SQL spelling is omitted to steer users.

Four NuGet packages: SqlArtisan (the builder, with the analyzer bundled inside — not shipped separately), SqlArtisan.ArrayBind (Oracle array-bind execution — one round trip per batch, not per row), SqlArtisan.Dapper (sync/async Dapper execution extensions), SqlArtisan.TableClassGen (console tool that generates table classes from a live database).

Terminology: 'table class' (a DbTableBase subclass), never 'table schema class'; 'query builder', not 'SQL builder'. Public factory names mirror SQL tokens with underscores as the only word boundaries (ADD_MONTHS → AddMonths, DATEADD → Dateadd).
Canonical documentation is llms.txt and docs/ in the repository; if this wiki and those files disagree, the repository documentation is authoritative.

The user-facing reference lives in docs/ (query-statements.md, expressions.md, functions.md, analyzer.md, cookbook.md, comparison.md, versioning.md, guides/) and the design decisions in docs/adr/. Each wiki page should explain how the code implements what those files describe and link to them, not restate per-dialect support tables, version floors or analyzer rule lists, which change between releases.

pages.title: Overview
pages.purpose: What SqlArtisan is and is not: a type-safe C# query builder that emits the SQL you write plus its bind parameters, with cross-database portability as a deliberate non-goal. Introduce the four packages, the five dialects and the guard-rail mission of ADR 0010, map the repository layout (src/, tests/, docs/, docs/adr/), and say where SqlArtisan sits among other .NET query builders and when not to choose it, following README.md and docs/comparison.md.

pages.title: Design Principles and ADRs
pages.purpose: Summarize the decisions in docs/adr/ that shape the code: faithful output (0001), dialect differences in the dialect layer (0002), automatic parameterization (0004), the Sql partial class (0005), allocation-light building (0006), the validity boundary (0007, 0011, 0012), the guard-rail mission (0010) and the one public namespace (0027). Explain what each rules out.

pages.title: Getting Started
pages.purpose: The path a new user takes: install the packages, generate table classes with TableClassGen, build a first statement and run it through SqlArtisan.Dapper (docs/guides/dapper-quickstart.md and README.md). Then the path for writing SqlArtisan with an AI coding assistant (docs/guides/ai-assistants.md): the llms.txt and llms-full.txt feed, setting the analyzer's target dialect, keeping table classes in step with the database, pinning each query with an exact-SQL test, and the rules snippet for an agent file.

pages.title: Building Statements
pages.purpose: How a statement is assembled: the static partial class Sql (src/SqlArtisan/Sql/Sql.{A..Y}.cs) as the entry point, builder stages under src/SqlArtisan/Internal/SqlBuilder, and the stage interfaces under src/SqlArtisan/SqlBuilder that make an invalid fluent chain fail to compile through its return type. docs/query-statements.md is the per-statement reference, and docs/cookbook.md shows realistic end-to-end queries, each pinned by an exact-SQL unit test.

pages.title: SELECT Queries
pages.purpose: SELECT, FROM, JOIN (including ON/USING pairing), WHERE, GROUP BY / HAVING, ORDER BY, set operators, FOR UPDATE and pagination, as SelectBuilder implements them. Use docs/query-statements.md for the user-facing shape.

pages.title: INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and MERGE
pages.purpose: The DML builders under src/SqlArtisan/Internal/SqlBuilder (Insert/, Update/, Delete/, Merge/): INSERT (VALUES, multiple rows, SET-like, INSERT ... SELECT), UPSERT forms, MERGE, correlated and joined UPDATE / DELETE, RETURNING, RETURNING INTO and OUTPUT. Cover InsertBuilder, UpdateBuilder, DeleteBuilder, MergeBuilder and DmlJoinState, and link the DELETE, UPDATE and INSERT sections of docs/query-statements.md.

pages.title: Common Table Expressions
pages.purpose: WITH and WITH RECURSIVE through WithBuilder (src/SqlArtisan/Internal/SqlBuilder/With) and CommonTableExpression (src/SqlArtisan/Internal/SqlPart/Clause/With), how a CTE body is rendered as its own query block, and the WITH section of docs/query-statements.md.

pages.title: Rendering and Bind Parameters
pages.purpose: How Build() turns parts into SQL text: SqlBuilderBase.BuildCore, SqlBuildingBuffer (pooled char buffer, parameter list, marker reuse for the same BindValue instance), BindValue and implicit binding, SqlStatement and SqlParameters. Note the allocation-light constraints of ADR 0006 and link the Bind Parameter Types section of docs/functions.md.

pages.title: Build-Time Validation
pages.purpose: What Build() and the stage methods reject and why: the duplicate-clause walk in SqlBuilderBase, the guards under src/SqlArtisan/Internal/SqlBuilder/Validation, the correlated-DML target guard, and the eager-versus-Build() timing rule in .claude/rules/guards-and-empty-states.md.

pages.title: Dialect Layer
pages.purpose: IDbmsDialect and its five implementations under src/SqlArtisan/Internal/SqlBuilder/DbmsDialect, DbmsResolver and SqlArtisanConfig.DefaultDbms, and how a construct one dialect lacks is exposed as its own API rather than rewritten (ADR 0001, 0002).

pages.title: Expressions and Functions
pages.purpose: How values and expressions are modeled: SqlPart, SqlExpression and SqlCondition, operator overloads, ExpressionResolver, and the public types under src/SqlArtisan/SqlPart, including the table references under SqlPart/TableReference (table classes, CTEs, derived, VALUES and UNNEST tables). docs/expressions.md and docs/functions.md are the user-facing reference.

pages.title: Operators, Conditions and Subqueries
pages.purpose: Arithmetic, comparison, logical AND/OR, IN, BETWEEN, LIKE, NULL handling, CASE, CAST, scalar subqueries, ALL/ANY/SOME, JSON, array, vector and full-text operators, as docs/expressions.md describes them.

pages.title: Function Catalog
pages.purpose: Function node classes, grouped by category folder under src/SqlArtisan/Internal/SqlPart/Expression/Function and, for the nodes ADR 0027 keeps public, under src/SqlArtisan/SqlPart/Expression/Function; list the categories as those folders name them rather than from memory. Cover the uncategorized nodes too, including NamedFunction, the Function(name, ...) form for a function SqlArtisan has no factory for, how a function is added (the sa-add-sql-function skill's six touch points), and every section of docs/functions.md.

pages.title: Window Functions and Aggregates
pages.purpose: OVER, PARTITION BY, frames, FILTER (WHERE ...), WITHIN GROUP and string aggregation: the AnalyticFunction, AggregateFunction, StringAggregateFunction and OrderedSetAggregateFunction folders under src/SqlArtisan/Internal/SqlPart/Expression/Function and src/SqlArtisan/SqlPart/Expression/Function, and the Window Functions, Conditional Aggregation and String Aggregation sections of docs/expressions.md. A bare analytic function is no SqlExpression until .Over() completes it, so a position typed SqlExpression rejects it at compile time; a position typed object (the select list, a function argument, a comparison operand) compiles, and the call that receives it throws an ArgumentException.

pages.title: The Analyzer
pages.purpose: The Roslyn analyzer in src/SqlArtisan.Analyzers, bundled inside the SqlArtisan package: how it is enabled through .editorconfig, its four ID bands (Configuration, Dialect, Schema, Validity; ADR 0018) and how a diagnostic is raised. docs/analyzer.md is the user-facing reference and holds the rule list.

pages.title: Dialect Matrix and Version Bounds
pages.purpose: DialectMatrix.cs, MatrixKey, VersionBounds, ContextRules and DialectUsageAnalyzer in src/SqlArtisan.Analyzers: how a construct is resolved to a support verdict per dialect and version (ADR 0013, 0015, 0021), how the sweep tests in tests/SqlArtisan.IntegrationTests/Tests/MatrixSweepTests.cs verify the matrix against live engines, and the version-aware and context-rule sections of docs/analyzer.md.

pages.title: Schema-Aware and Validity Rules
pages.purpose: The rules in src/SqlArtisan.Analyzers that read the DbColumnMetadata attributes TableClassGen emits (the SQLA02xx band) and the validity rules (SQLA03xx): what each collects from the code, ADR 0010's limits on what a schema rule may conclude, and the matching sections of docs/analyzer.md.

pages.title: Analyzer Configuration
pages.purpose: AnalyzerConfigResolver and DialectTargetSet in src/SqlArtisan.Analyzers: the sqlartisan_syntax_* keys (ADR 0019) and the override keys (ADR 0008), configuration errors reported as SQLA0001 (ADR 0025), the stability contract of ADR 0026, and the Enabling It and override-key sections of docs/analyzer.md.

pages.title: Execution and Tooling
pages.purpose: The packages beside the core builder (src/SqlArtisan.Dapper, src/SqlArtisan.ArrayBind, src/SqlArtisan.TableClassGen): how a built SqlStatement is executed and how table classes are kept in step with the database.

pages.title: Dapper Integration
pages.purpose: src/SqlArtisan.Dapper: the SqlMapper sync and async extensions, SqlParametersExtensions.ToDynamicParameters, type handlers and value converters. Follow docs/guides/dapper-quickstart.md.

pages.title: Oracle Array Bind
pages.purpose: SqlArtisan.ArrayBind: running one statement for N rows in one round trip through ODP.NET array binding, and its limits. Follow docs/guides/oracle-array-bind.md.

pages.title: TableClassGen
pages.purpose: src/SqlArtisan.TableClassGen: reading each engine's catalog (Catalog/), emitting table classes with schema metadata (Generation/), the argument-driven CLI (Cli/), and drift detection with --check and --fix. Follow src/SqlArtisan.TableClassGen/README.md and the command-line section of docs/versioning.md.

pages.title: Verification and Quality
pages.purpose: How correctness is pinned: exact-SQL unit tests in tests/SqlArtisan.Tests, analyzer tests in tests/SqlArtisan.Analyzers.Tests, the integration matrix against live engines via Testcontainers in tests/SqlArtisan.IntegrationTests, the combinatorial PICT and CsCheck tests under tests/SqlArtisan.IntegrationTests/Randomized, mutation testing, and the CI workflows in .github/workflows.

pages.title: Performance and Benchmarks
pages.purpose: tests/SqlArtisan.Benchmark: the BenchmarkDotNet comparison against other .NET query builders, what it measures, why the allocation column is the firm one, and the build-path techniques ADR 0006 allows. Follow tests/SqlArtisan.Benchmark/README.md, the performance section of README.md and docs/comparison.md.

pages.title: Versioning and Releases
pages.purpose: docs/versioning.md (what the public API and the analyzer contract are, what counts as breaking), package validation against the last release, CHANGELOG.md and the release procedure in CLAUDE.md.
